scenario_narratives.base: The 2026 Canadian wireless price war grinds on but does not escalate: service revenue grows ~2-3% a year after the FY2026 MLSE annualisation, with low immigration capping postpaid net adds (380k FY2024 -> 145k FY2025) and mobile ARPU drifting down, offset by Cable internet/Xfinity bundling and sports/media-rights growth. Adjusted EBITDA margin holds ~43.5-44% as residual Shaw synergies roughly offset ARPU pressure and Media mix dilution. The FY2026 capex cut is mostly deferral: capex plus spectrum reverts to ~15.5% of revenue by FY2029. Leverage drifts down from 3.8x on free cash flow; the MLSE buyout closes in Q4 2026 and a minority sale of Rogers Sports happens at something close to the Kilmer-implied value.
scenario_narratives.bull: Big-3 pricing discipline returns by 2027 (the pattern after prior Canadian price wars), CRTC fee/MVNO rules prove less damaging than feared, and Rogers' network-quality lead (most reliable 5G, Satellite-to-mobile) supports ARPU. Margins expand to ~45.5% on completed Shaw synergies and MLSE/NHL-rights economics; capex settles at ~14.5% including spectrum, so the FY2026 capital-efficiency step is partly permanent. Revenue compounds ~3% organically. The Rogers Sports minority stake is sold at or above C$25bn total value, crystallising the franchise excess and cutting leverage toward 3.0x, with a re-rating to an 18x FCF / ~7.5x EBITDA terminal.
scenario_narratives.bear: The flanker-brand price war (Fizz, Lucky, Freedom) becomes structural: the CRTC switching-fee ban, mandated MVNO access and broadcasting levies push mobile ARPU down further, cable video/home phone keep shrinking, and organic revenue is near-flat for three years. Margins compress to ~41.5%. The FY2026 capex cut proves to be deferral, returning with interest (5G-Advanced, DOCSIS 4.0, the next spectrum auction) to ~16.5% plus spectrum. With leverage still ~4x after the C$4.35bn short-term-funded MLSE buyout, S&P cuts to junk, refinancing costs rise, and the sports minority sale slips or prices well below C$25bn. Terminal 14x FCF (~6x EBITDA).

valuation_philosophy.summary: Unlevered owner-FCF DCF on Rogers' consolidated operations at a single CAD WACC, with every claim ahead of the common (hedged debt, 100% of hybrids, the MLSE put, the BNSI preferred-like NCI) deducted once, leases charged in the flows, and a deliberately haircut sum-of-parts credit for sports franchises whose transaction values sit far above their cash-flow capitalisation. Equity is a thin slice (~30%) of enterprise value, so every 1% of EV moves the per-share value ~3%; the dispersion between scenarios is the honest result of that leverage, not modelling noise.
key_risks_to_valuation: Leverage: ~C$51bn of claims ahead of the common (ex leases) against a ~C$23bn market cap - a 10% EV miss is ~C$14/share
Capex reversion: the FY2026 guide (~11.5% of revenue) vs the 17-20% history; each 1pp of revenue in perpetuity is ~C$9/share
Sports-value credit (C$10.65/share) depends on franchise valuations staying near 2025-26 deal levels and on Rogers actually monetising
Wireless price war and CRTC policy (switching-fee ban, MVNO access) on ARPU
Refinancing: 2025-26 hybrids at 6.25-7.125%; a downgrade to sub-investment-grade would raise the cost of the 94.6% fixed-rate book as it rolls

inputs.share_count_basis: Diluted weighted average 540m (Q2 2026 note 10; Class A ~111m + Class B ~429m participate equally in dividends above 5c and are valued as one class). Held FLAT: SBC is expensed in the flows; no buybacks since 2019; the DRIP issued Class B shares only in Q1 2025 and has been cash-only since. No non-SBC issuance modelled.
inputs.debt_basis: Bonds/notes/loans at face 40,804 (LTD 35,191 + current 4,855 + deferred costs 758) less 2,122 adjustment of USD debt to hedged CAD rate = 38,682; plus short-term borrowings 2,237 and CIB deferred grant 78 = 40,997. Subordinated hybrid notes taken at 100% (NOT the 50% rating-agency equity credit Rogers uses in its 38,006 'adjusted net debt'): they rank ahead of the common. Lease liabilities (3,415) EXCLUDED here because leases are charged in the flows (treatment B). Source: Q2 2026 MD&A adjusted net debt table, lines 1226-1245.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 annual report note 29 / cash flow add-back: SBC 98m (incl. equity-derivative effect). Rogers awards are largely cash-settled and hedged with equity derivatives; SBC sits inside operating costs and is NOT added back in adjusted EBITDA, so it is already a cash cost in the company's EBITDA. No equity-award tax line (cash settlement). Shown explicitly at ~0.45% of revenue with the EBITDA path grossed up by the same amount, so it is charged once.
inputs.price_as_of: 2026-10-09T20:00:00Z regular close (TSX), Yahoo Finance chart API
inputs.wacc_rationale: CAD build, one rate for all scenarios (risk is in the scenario flows, not stacked on the rate). Rf 10y GoC ~3.3%, ERP 5.0%. Unlevered telecom beta ~0.45 relevered at market D/E ~2.3x (debt + hybrids + MLSE put + BNSI NCI vs a ~C$23bn market cap) gives beta ~1.2 and cost of equity ~9.4%; pre-tax senior cost of debt ~5.3% (BBB-, recent hybrids 6.25-7.125%), after-tax ~3.9%. Market-weight WACC computes to ~5.6%; 6.5% used because that mechanical figure leans on a capital structure the S&P Negative outlook says is not sustainable, and because equity-heavier long-run weights (management targets leverage well below 3.8x) raise it. Sensitivity grid shows 4.5-8.5%.
inputs.lease_treatment: Treatment (B), leases as operating cost: lease principal + interest (FY2025 559 + 147 = 706, 3.25% of revenue; H1 2026 297 + 80 annualising to ~3.3%) deducted inside the flows via lease_cost_pct_path; lease liabilities (3,415 at 30-Jun-2026) EXCLUDED from net debt. D&A path for cash tax excludes right-of-use depreciation (455 in FY2025).
inputs.nci_treatment: Flows are 100% consolidated (adjusted EBITDA includes all of BNSI and MLSE). NCI charged ONCE in the bridge: (1) BNSI (Blackstone-led backhaul network subsidiary, 2025 network transaction) NCI at book 6,291 - it carries an 8% USD distribution hedged to 7.16% CAD (~C$466m/yr, 116-117m/qtr in 2026), a debt-like claim; (2) MLSE 25% Kilmer stake via the 4,350 put liability = agreed cash purchase price (closing Q4 2026, funded with short-term credit). After paying it Rogers owns 100% of MLSE, consistent with 100% MLSE flows. FY2025 'distributions to NCI' 133 are therefore not deducted again from the flows.
inputs.non_operating_treatment: Excluded from normalized earnings and from the flows: Q3 2025 C$4,976m non-cash gain on remeasuring the prior 37.5% MLSE stake; Q2 2026 C$1,034m non-cash loss on revaluing the MLSE put liability (3.3bn -> 4.35bn); 151m gain on debt repurchase; 69m data-centre disposal gain; subsidiary-equity-derivative FV moves. FY2025 reported EPS 12.74 and Q2 2026 EPS -1.37 are both distorted by these and are not used. Restructuring, acquisition and other (439 FY2025, 406 FY2024, 260 H1 2026) IS charged: it has run every year since 2016 (139-685m) and Rogers' own FCF adds it back; it is deducted inside the EBITDA path at 1.8% of revenue FY2026, gliding to 0.8%.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF DCF, component route, with the non-US adaptations (CAD WACC, lease treatment B, NCI in the bridge, matching-asset rule for associates, sum-of-parts credit for sports franchises). Rogers is a capital-intensive operating telecom - routing-table row 'operating company, non-US' - not a bank/REIT/holdco. First valuation; no prior model. BASE YEAR: FY2025 revenue 21,712 includes MLSE only from 1-Jul-2025, so FY2026 growth (5.5% base) carries the MLSE annualisation (H1 2026 revenue +8.9% YoY, Media +65%) on top of 3-5% service-revenue guidance; growth from FY2027 is organic. SHAW BREAK: FY2023 revenue +25% and debt +23bn are acquisition step-changes; historical 3/5yr CAGRs are not used as forward rates - pre-Shaw organic revenue CAGR FY2016-19 was 3.2%. CAPEX: FY2026 guidance cut to C$2.5-2.7bn (~11.5% of revenue vs 17-20% over 2016-2025) is used for year 1 only; the cut is attributed by management to competitive intensity and regulatory decisions (deferrals/cancellations), so base reverts to 15.5% by FY2029 including ~1pp/yr for spectrum licences, which sit outside reported capex (3500MHz 2021 C$3.3bn, 3800MHz 2023 C$0.5bn). The FY2026 FCF guidance raise (3.3-3.5bn -> 4.1-4.3bn) is therefore treated as largely timing, not a new run-rate. Rogers' reported FCF (3,356 FY2025) is post-interest but excludes restructuring cash, lease principal, NCI distributions and working capital; reported_fcf here is OCF - capex (2,352), last_fcf = that less SBC (2,254) and is levered/informational - the engine projects UNLEVERED flows from components. Unlevered FY2025 owner FCF reconstructs to ~C$3.7bn (EBITDA 9,820 - restructuring 439 - leases 706 - unlevered cash tax ~1,250 - capex 3,707). Cash tax 25% on EBIT ex-ROU, ex-Shaw-FV-increment D&A calibrates to FY2025: actual cash tax 700 + interest shield ~540 = ~1,250 unlevered. WC capture -15% of revenue increase (device financing receivables and payables unwind consumed 592/876m in FY2025/24; Rogers excludes it from its FCF). SPORTS: the flows capitalise Media (TTM EBITDA ~365m on ~4.1bn revenue) at ~3bn, against an arm's-length 2026 price for 25% of MLSE of 4.35bn (100% = C$17.4bn) and management's '>$25bn' Rogers Sports estimate; the bridge credits 40% of the MLSE-only excess (17.4bn - ~3bn = ~14.4bn -> 5.75bn, ~C$10.65/share). Blue Jays, Rogers Centre and Sportsnet get NO excess credit. Without this item every IV is ~C$10.65/share lower.
inputs.historical_growth_notes: SBC-adjusted (owner) FCF CAGR (2.95% 5yr) is in line with reported (3.2%): SBC is small and cash-settled, not a growth subsidy here.

bear.ebitda_margin_note: Adjusted margin 43.2 -> 41.5%: flanker-brand price war persists, CRTC switching-fee ban (TRP 2026-43) and MVNO wholesale access erode wireless pricing, cord-cutting continues; restructuring stays ~1% of revenue.
bear.capex_note: 2026 deferrals come back with interest; 5G-Advanced/DOCSIS 4.0 and the next spectrum auction push capex+spectrum back to the 2016-2025 average (~17%).

base.ebitda_margin_note: Adjusted EBITDA margin 43.5% FY2026 (guided EBITDA +1-3% on revenue +5-6% = full-year MLSE mix dilution), 43.5/43.7/43.8/44.0% thereafter on residual Shaw synergies offsetting price-war ARPU pressure (mobile ARPU 58.06 Q1-24 -> 54.25 Q2-26). Path = adjusted margin + 0.45pp SBC gross-up - restructuring (1.8% FY26, 1.2% FY27, 0.8% from FY28).
base.da_note: Tax-relevant D&A: FY2025 book 4,802 less ROU 455 less ~829 non-deductible Shaw fair-value increment = ~16.2-17%; glides to the capex run-rate.
base.capex_note: FY2026 guided C$2.5-2.7bn; reverts toward 14.5% network capex + ~1pp spectrum licences (outside reported capex).
base.terminal_cap_rationale: 17x unlevered owner FCF ~ 7.0x terminal EBITDA, about today's lease-inclusive EV/EBITDA (~7.7x) - no multiple expansion assumed. Gordon at 6.5%/2.0% would be ~22.7x.

bull.ebitda_margin_note: Adjusted margin 43.7 -> 45.5% by FY2030 as the price war burns out (Big-3 discipline returns), Shaw synergies complete and MLSE playoff/media-rights economics lift Media margins.

entry_price.note: All three hurdle entry prices are NEGATIVE (base -18.32): at a 15% rate applied to the unlevered flows, EV (~C$35bn base) is below the ~C$43bn of net claims ahead of the common, so no positive price earns 15% on this method. This is the leverage talking, not a bug: the base value is C$33 at a 9% required return, ~C$19 at 10% and ~C$0 at 12% (required_return_table). Read it as: the stock only clears a high hurdle via the levered equity return if the deleveraging and sports monetisation happen, i.e. the bull case.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 17x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised to 30% from the 15% default: BBB- with Negative outlook, ~4x leverage before the short-term-funded C$4.35bn MLSE buyout, a sector-wide 2026 price war (TD downgrade of all three incumbents) and a regulator actively working against incumbent pricing. Base 50% because guidance (service revenue +3-5%, EBITDA +1-3%) has been held through the price war and FCF is tracking the raised range. Bull cut to 20% because it needs several independent things to go right at once - pricing discipline, permanent capex efficiency, and a sports monetisation at a full price.
probability_weighted.band_note: House and street differ only by Rogers' small, cash-settled SBC (~0.45% of revenue), so the band is ~C$4/share wide and the price sits well BELOW both ends; band_position of about -400% is the arithmetic of a narrow band, not a regime reading. The market is pricing neither basis but a discount to both.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
